items.title: Harry Kane claims men’s Ballon d’Or to end England’s 25-year wait for winner
items.summary: Alexia Putellas picks up women’s award for third time England captain acclaimed in London ceremony Harry Kane is the Ballon d’Or winner for 2026, the first Englishman to win football’s most prestigious individual trophy in 25 years. Two hours into a lavishly excitable ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London, Kane’s name emerged from the final envelope to wild cheers inside the auditorium. The women’s Ballon d’Or, awarded moments earlier, was won by Alexia Putellas of London City Lionesses, a third Ballon, five years on from her first in the colours of Barcelona. Continue reading...

items.title: England Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegation
items.summary: Match in new Fifa competition abandoned England players refuse to resume match England abandoned their Under-15 World Cup match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. Fifa confirmed it was investigating what happened in the final minute of the Group C fixture in Baku, Azerbaijan, when Ireland were leading 4-1. Footage showed an England player approaching the bench after an altercation. He is believed to have alleged an opponent called him a “monkey” and raised a complaint with the coaching staff, prompting England’s head coach, Matt Thorpe, to approach the referee. items.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
items.summary: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qué?, the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

items.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
items.summary: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager. Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here. Continue reading...

De Brusselaars gingen met zware 4-0-cijfers onderuit op het veld van KAA Gent. Philippe Albert nuanceert die uitslag, maar ziet tegelijk dezelfde problemen terugkeren bij paars-wit.

items.title: L'entraîneur de l'Atalanta fait une déclaration surprenante sur De Ketelaere, Capello en rajoute une couche
items.summary: Charles De Ketelaere vit une saison difficile à l'Atalanta. Le Diable Rouge attend toujours son premier but en Serie A et fait face à des critiques de plus en plus nombreuses. Pourtant, Maurizio Sarri continue de croire en lui. « Nous attendons beaucoup de Charles. Il possède un énorme potentiel et nous continuons à croire en lui. Mais il doit commencer à se montrer décisif », a-t-il clairement déclaré.

items.title: Complete chaos bij Gouden Bal: plots drie winnaars aangekondigd en organisatie moet ingrijpen
items.summary: De organisatie van de Gouden Bal heeft maandagavond voor enorme verwarring gezorgd. Enkele uren voor de uitreiking van de prestigieuze prijs verschenen op de officiële website liefst drie verschillende artikels waarin telkens een andere speler als winnaar werd aangekondigd. Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé en Lamine Yamal mochten zich daardoor even winnaar van de Ballon d'Or noemen, maar al snel bleek dat er iets grondig was misgelopen.
